meta.title: m to in Converter — Meter to Inch
meta.description: Convert Meter (m) to Inch (in) instantly. 1 m = 39.370079 in. Free, accurate, browser-based.

content.intro: Convert meters (m) to inches (in) instantly. Both measure length, so the relationship is strictly linear: each meter equals 39.370079 inches. Use the converter above for any value, or read on for the formula, a quick lookup table, and practical tips.
content.result_section: One meter is equal to **39.370079 inches**. To go the other way, one inch equals **0.0254 meters**. For everyday use, rounding to 2–4 decimal places is usually enough; for engineering or scientific work, keep the full precision shown by the converter.
content.formula_section:
The conversion is a single multiplication:

> inches = meters × 39.370079

Worked example — converting 10 meters:

10 × 39.370079 = **393.70079 in**.

To invert, divide by 39.370079 (or multiply by 0.0254).
content.use_cases:
- Cooking and recipe conversions when switching between metric and imperial measurements.
- Travel planning where signage and maps use different unit systems.
- DIY and home-improvement projects that mix metric materials with imperial tools.
- Fitness tracking when devices report in one system and goals are set in another.
- Shipping and logistics where weight and dimensions drive cost.
content.tips:
Keep the factor handy: 1 m ≈ 39.370079 in. For rough mental math, round to the nearest sensible digit.

Mind the units. Meter and Inch both measure length; squared or cubic variants need a different factor (factor², factor³).

When precision matters (engineering, lab work, dosing), avoid rounding mid-calculation — convert once at the final step using the full factor.
content.faq:
**Q:** How many inches are in 1 meter?
**A:** 39.370079 inches.

**Q:** What's the formula to convert m to in?
**A:** inches = meters × 39.370079.

**Q:** How do I convert in back to m?
**A:** Multiply by 0.0254 (or divide by 39.370079).

**Q:** Is rounding to 2 decimal places accurate enough?
**A:** For most everyday uses, yes. For scientific or engineering work, use the full precision from the converter.

**Q:** Does this m to in converter work offline?
**A:** Yes — all math runs in your browser, no network required after the page loads.
